messages:
vivian: quick heads-up — I'm bringing up a new reranker candidate (v2-small-ptq) on the staging holdout. before we run the full bench, need to decide how we handle multi-reference queries + metric aggregation. seeing odd signal: NDCG@10 barely changes but MRR@1 drops for some slices. anyone against a short protocol proposal?

ashok: +1 for protocol. question: do we treat multiple references as separate positive labels (i.e., any-match) or aggregate graded relevance?

sara: i'd prefer a weighted-refs approach — average label across refs so docs with 3/5 refs get partial credit. avoids binary masking of near-duplicates. also stratify by query type (narrow vs broad).

kevin: if we average refs we should pick a stable aggregator for MRR. MRR is sensitive to top-1 ties — maybe use a soft tiebreaker: rank_score = (1 / (rank + eps)) and aggregate over sampled permutations. simpler: compute pairwise win-rate across docs to get significance for top1.

vivian: good points. my concerns: (1) our holdout is small for tail queries so bootstrap CI needed, (2) quantization might reorder docs that differ only on punctuation/casing -> candidate normalisation matters. proposal below.

vivian: proposed short protocol: 
1) run eval on two datasets: a) multiref-anchors (3 refs) with averaged relevance, b) multi-match (binary any-match) as sensitivity check.
2) compute metrics: NDCG@5/10, MRR@1, and pairwise win-rate@1.
3) bootstrap 1000 resamples at query-level to get 95% CIs and p-values.
4) slice by query length (<=6 tokens, 7-20, >20), doc length quartiles, and candidate-dup flag.
5) run casefold vs preserve casing preproc to check tokeniser-induced shifts.

ashok: sounds sane. small nit: bootstrap at query-level but preserve candidate pool per query. also include a per-query weight option (uniform vs traffic-weighted) in the reports.

sara: adding: record per-query label entropy (across refs) and report metric correlations vs entropy. hypothesis: high-entropy queries will show larger MRR variance under PTQ.

kevin: can someone add a quick smoke run command for CI? i can kick off cluster for int8 runs.

vivian: sure — smoke command we use: ```bash
run_eval --model v2-small-ptq --holdout "2026-03-01..2026-03-15" --datasets multiref-anchors,multi-match --metrics ndcg@5,ndcg@10,mrr@1,winrate@1 --bootstrap 1000 --slices qlen,docq,dupflag --preproc casefold,preserve --output /tmp/v2ptq-smoke.json
```

eval-bot: quick summary (from /tmp/v2ptq-smoke.json, 1000 bootstrap): 
- multiref-anchors (avg-refs): NDCG@10 delta -0.7% (CI [-1.5%, +0.1%], p=0.08)
- multiref-anchors: MRR@1 delta -2.1% (CI [-3.4%, -0.8%], p=0.02)
- multi-match (binary): NDCG@10 delta -0.2% (CI [-1.0%, +0.6%], p=0.28)
- slice (<=6 tokens): MRR@1 delta -4.8% (CI [-7.1%, -2.2%], p<0.01)
- casefold vs preserve: top1 changes concentrated in short queries and punctuation-heavy docs.

vivian: thanks eval-bot. that pattern matches my local run. short queries and punctuation seem to be the PTQ regression surface. likely tokenizer rounding/quant noise leading to reordering.

ashok: action items: (1) run per-layer quantization ablation (only attention weights vs full linear), (2) run candidate normalisation pass (strip punctuation + canonicalise whitespace) and re-eval, (3) compute per-query logit-gap distribution to see if top1 flips are low-margin. I'll take (1) and (3).

sara: i'll run the casefold + punctuation-normalise preproc and re-run multiref-anchors. tagging @kevin for cluster time.

kevin: ack — reserving two nodes for 4h window. will start the int8 ablation once ashok pushes configs.

vivian: one more ask — when we publish the report, include both avg-refs and binary any-match tables + per-slice bootstrap CIs, and a short note about how ref-aggregation choices change p-values. helps reviewers understand the apparent metric mismatch.

ashok: agree. also include a small appendix showing a couple example queries where doc order flips — helps debugging.

vivian: perfect. i'll create a short runbook in the rerank-evals repo and link it here when done. thanks all :) :thumbsup:
